basis: Aortic aneurysms and arterial tortuosity with frequent skeletal disease: disc degeneration 3/4, scoliosis 5/12; bruising and striae do not establish additional organ damage.
Reported syndrome combines congenital cardiac malformation, extensive skeletal dysplasia and intellectual disability; phenotype frequencies are unspecified.
Inherited ventricular arrhythmia; no other directly affected organ established.
Neurodevelopmental impairment and musculoskeletal abnormalities define the syndrome; intellectual disability 22/29 and joint hypermobility 17/32; strabismus only 3/30.
Multinodular enlargement of the thyroid gland.
Congenital narrowing or absence of the coronary artery ostium.
Benign cystic inflammatory changes of the renal pelvis and ureter; infection or autoimmunity is not inherent.
Autoimmune cutaneous sclerosis with defining vasculopathy; esophageal dysfunction is a cardinal feature and occurs in most. Pulmonary damage is not universal across CREST.
Ichthyosis, alopecia, ectropion and intellectual disability define the syndrome; absent additional neurologic changes does not negate intellectual disability.
Inherited infantile epilepsy; ictal apnea and cyanosis do not establish pulmonary damage.
Noncirrhotic hepatic portal vascular disease causes portal hypertension; varices remain vascular, and congestive splenomegaly alone does not establish blood-organ damage.
Sensorineural deafness and progressive retinal degeneration define Usher syndrome; vestibular dysfunction is otologic, and additional brain disease is occasional.
Nail and pilar-cyst disorder; ocular inflammation 80-99% and blepharitis 30-79% support eye involvement. Renal calculi are a separately diagnosed disease.
Recurrent dislocation of the proximal fibula affects the locomotor system.
Asymptomatic dengue virus infection; no organ damage is established by this subtype.
Congenital pancreatic cyst is a structural pancreatic lesion without defining endocrine dysfunction; jaundice and pancreatitis are occasional.
Progressive skeletal dysplasia and intellectual disability define the syndrome; both are documented in 5/5 patients. Proptosis and ear shape alone do not establish dysfunction.
Primary carcinoma arises in the urinary bladder; advanced stage does not establish any particular additional organ as commonly occupied.
Congenital red-cell destruction; jaundice and dark urine reflect hemolysis rather than intrinsic hepatic or renal injury.
Cortical malformation and micromelia define the syndrome; hypoparathyroidism is annotated at 30-79%, though the definition notes one case. Fetal pyelectasis alone is insufficient.
Autoimmune small-vessel vasculitis; glomerulonephritis 80-99%, pulmonary capillaritis/hemorrhage ~30-50%. Neuropathy, GI injury and skin ulcers also qualify but are omitted at the cap.
Inherited susceptibility specifically concerns noise-induced cochlear hearing loss; susceptibility alone does not establish existing hearing damage.
Congenital craniosynostosis affects skull sutures; maternal thyroid disease does not establish an endocrine disorder in the affected child.
Ovarian reproductive stromal neoplasm; this umbrella includes nonsecretory fibromas, and endocrine dysfunction is not defining across the group.
Isolated developmental optic nerve abnormality with visual impairment in 8/8; optic nerve is ocular. Unrelated carcinoma ancestors do not establish additional disease sites.
